key_facts: Canon is F0 (record envelope), F1 (backends seam), R0 (block round-trip), R1 (surface renderer), R2 (vault mirror + SOUL.md), V2 (drift + writing gate), V3 (persona-thesis assessor), V4 (reconcile band) — all built; M4 is the next band after V4. Source: CLAUDE.md build state.

Python 3.11+; standard library only; no runtime dependencies; TDD; no source file over 300 lines; no function over 50 lines; branch before committing; do not push/PR/deploy without explicit go (CLAUDE.md:208-216).

F1 MemoryBackend Protocol is the shape M4 leg 1 imitates: capability tokens, record_key/split_key, guard_put refusal on kind mismatch or record-enforceable dropped capability, injected duck-typed store handle, engine imports forbidden (CLAUDE.md:33-40).

R2 vault codec is the shape M4 leg 2 completes the read half of: render_note projects a record to a whole markdown file with frontmatter carrier + heading + per-kind body + `## canon links` trailer; ingest_note reconstructs from the JSON carrier alone so a hand-edited body never changes the record (CLAUDE.md:88-93).

Vault path names a note by digest of (scope, id) so a hostile id cannot forge one; a file that is not a canon note is off-limits and never clobbered; a stale note is orphan-reported and never deleted (CLAUDE.md:92-97).

Frontmatter codec emits a fixed set of single-quoted scalars and one authoritative `canon:` key carrying record.to_json() verbatim; no YAML loader runs on ingest so the `!!python/object` trap is inert (CLAUDE.md:84-87).

Design doc is APPROVED FOR IMPLEMENTATION PLANNING (2026-08-30); approval does not authorize edits to I0, publication, deployment, package registration, provider claims, or release work (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:3-7).
canon.capsule/v1 carries an explicit compatibility block: record_schema_min, capsule_schema, requires_features (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:183-187).

Determinism rule: identical source bytes, source declarations, compiler version, profile, target adapter descriptor, and budget config produce byte-identical capsule bytes (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:212).
Current package metadata is name='canon', version='0.0.0', Python >=3.11, FSL-1.1-MIT, no runtime dependencies, no console scripts (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:34).
Current record scopes are exactly `global` and `workspace`; `repo` is deliberately absent (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:37).
V4 already discloses D-58 (block filter, latent V2 mixed-pool defect) as an owed fix (CLAUDE.md:194).
m4_transport_requirements: Model after F1 MemoryBackend: a Protocol with capability tokens, guard_put-style refusal on record-enforceable dropped capability, and injected duck-typed handle — cite CLAUDE.md:33-40 — 'MemoryBackend Protocol, the five capability tokens, record_key/split_key, and guard_put'.

Adapters must publish one of four support tiers — Enforced, Native advisory, Guided, Unsupported — and no adapter may label advisory or guided behavior as enforced (SPEC-CANON-PILLAR-20260830.md:31-38).

Failure must expose whether it was caused by missing authority, unavailable local state, stale evidence, secret quarantine, conflict, incompatible budget, or unsupported host lifecycle (SPEC-CANON-PILLAR-20260830.md:38).

canon.adapter/v1 descriptor carries tier, evidence, import/export, hierarchy, lifecycle, limits, auth/privacy, known unknowns — 'No advertised tier above fixture proof' (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:432). Descriptor is a Wave 1 schema so M4 speaks its shape without shipping it.

Bootstrap adapters run read-only and root-confined by default; write, exec, network, plugin, or secrets access requires explicit policy and must appear in the witness (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:471).
Capsule target block encodes adapter/surface/integration_tier and a boolean `host_enforcement_observed` (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:168-174).
Determinism rule: adapter descriptor is one of the inputs the capsule bytes are keyed on; observed host behavior is a witness field, not a manifest field (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:212).

Concurrency contract: workspace/target-surface run locks, source-state digest captured before compile, compare-and-swap before write/import, append-only witnesses, stale-run abort on source change, distinct witnesses for concurrent chats, no partial success as clean, undo receipts (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:519-527).

Default-deny import: no external record, archive entry, generated instruction, or model summary becomes active until schema, trust, freshness, conflict, source-reachability, secret/PII, disclosure, and budget checks pass (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:467).

Trust labels the seam must speak: trusted-local, signed-pinned, signed-unknown-key, unsigned-local, imported-untrusted, model-synthesized-unreviewed, secret-quarantined, stale, public-exportable, private-local-only (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:477-486).

Freshness states the seam must distinguish: current, stale, superseded, contradictory, untrusted, unknown, blocked; a source that cannot be reached is `unknown` or `blocked`, never silently current (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:296-304).

FilesBackend-style blocker to prevent in the seam: reject paths derived from untrusted values before path derivation; reject `..`, separator-bearing strings, drive-qualified values, unknown scope names, alternate data streams, symlinks, junctions, reparse points, duplicate normalized names, case-fold collisions (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:246, 533).
Cross-machine and mobile review states must distinguish missing local path from missing record (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:461).
Reuse Emet/Flywheel/Relay patterns through small adapter seams; do not vendor or depend until license/API review (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:691).

Bootstrap state machine S0-S8 must be representable through the seam; witness must be append-only, path-clean, idempotent by run id, safe for public redaction, bound to source-state; Enforced starts fail closed if the witness cannot be written (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:313-322, 366-370).

Failure code vocabulary that hostile/quirky remotes may raise: unsupported_lifecycle, missing_authority, source_unreachable, index_unavailable, local_state_unavailable, secret_quarantine, stale_evidence, conflict, budget_incompatible, authority_untrusted, tier_mislabeled, source_changed, capsule_nondeterministic, critical_atom_loss, omission_invisible, presentation_unavailable, unsupported_content_type, readiness_failed, readiness_blocked, readiness_false_pass, witness_unavailable (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:313-322).
Honest nulls stay visible: Unknown, blocked, stale, untrusted, unsupported, and contradictory are different states (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:69).
Raw prompt, response, screen, microphone, and transcript capture is off by default; metadata-only recording remains visible and disableable (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:469).

Signatures prove integrity only until a pinned key, scope, expiry, replay, and source-state policy say they prove more; unknown-key signatures are integrity-only (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:67, 488).

Rescue/offline: emergency handoff `works offline from local state and marks remote-only sources unknown/blocked. Network-disabled fixture succeeds with visible omissions.' (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:434).

Symmetry with F1: sqlite is the zero-drop reference and mneme/flywheel adapters `map onto an injected, duck-typed store handle and import no engine` — the transport seam must not import a network engine either (CLAUDE.md:38-40).
m4_vault_frontend_requirements: Vault codec: render_note projects a record to a whole markdown file (frontmatter carrier, heading, per-kind body, `## canon links` trailer) and refuses any record it cannot faithfully project; ingest_note reconstructs the record from the carrier JSON alone (CLAUDE.md:88-93).
Identity-not-content names the file: the path digests the (scope, id) key so a hostile id cannot forge one (CLAUDE.md:92-93).
Off-limits and spoof refusals: a file that is not a canon note is off-limits and never clobbered (CLAUDE.md:95-97).
Orphan-reported never deleted: a stale note is reported as an orphan and never deleted (CLAUDE.md:97).
Vault carrier is lossless: its declared-drop ledger is empty and any field difference is an undeclared loss that fails the verdict closed (CLAUDE.md:98-100).

Frontmatter codec is constrained: fixed set of single-quoted scalars and one authoritative `canon:` key carrying record.to_json() verbatim; reads only that key back; no YAML loader runs on ingest so the `!!python/object` trap is inert (CLAUDE.md:84-87).

R2 D-23 through D-36 govern the vault legs including: constrained codec (no YAML loader), whole-file note carried by one JSON line, links from relations not body prose, hub reuses the surface sort key, authoritative carrier and one-way body, fixed frontmatter key order, identity-not-content, off-limits/spoof refusals, lexical vault containment, orphan reported never deleted, render-superset invariant, non-durable hub marker, vault is not a registry root-kind (CLAUDE.md:107-112).

Frontend must be the read half that closes a lossless round trip — current fidelity tools include `deterministic schema round trips, textblock/vault fidelity, drift checks, persona thesis basis checks, and V4 reconcile gates` (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:39).
Determinism carries through: render twice and compare bytes; digest/body drift detected (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:426).
Read side must remain total and read-only: V2 pattern established `both gates total and read-only` (D-42) — M4's frontend inherits this (CLAUDE.md:134-135).
Path-cleanliness: witnesses and run receipts are path-clean; no absolute host path emitted (CLAUDE.md:186-188).

.canonpack archive-safety controls carry to any read-side extraction/replay: parse manifest before extraction; reject absolute paths, `..`, drive-qualified paths, alternate data streams, symlinks, junctions, reparse points, duplicate normalized names, case-fold collisions, oversize files, decompression bombs, unsupported compression, and digest mismatch before any unsafe read/write; never auto-promote into startup instructions (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:243-248).

Default-deny import applies at ingest boundary: schema, trust, freshness, conflict, source-reachability, secret/PII, disclosure, and budget checks must all pass (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:467).

FilesBackend blocker analogue: validate scopes before path derivation; reject `..`, separator-bearing strings, drive-qualified values, or unknown scope names; prove no outside-root artifact is created (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:533).

Concurrency posture on the read side: source-state digest captured before compile; compare-and-swap before write/import; stale-run abort on source change; append-only witnesses (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:519-527).

Disclosure profiles: Full local, Project only, No secrets, Team-safe, Public-safe, Need-to-know; every profile must show included/excluded counts, reasons, and source ids; a critical atom excluded by a disclosure profile fails the build or requires explicit operator resolution (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:494-501).
Redact and classify before model exposure, export, or logging; redaction is not permission to read protected files (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:468).
Local-first and reversible: preview before writes, write only approved Canon-owned regions or artifacts, record undo receipts, avoid deleting user material (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:65).

Accessibility contract: keyboard-only, screen-reader structure, no color-only state, WCAG 2.2 AA target, NO_COLOR/--no-color, plain-language primary UI, localization-ready, distinguish missing local path from missing record (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:451-461).

Retention concerns for the read side: sensitivity labels per atom/record, tombstone records, purge receipts, derived-surface deletion coverage across SQLite, files, vault, managed surfaces, capsules, `.canonpack`, witnesses, backups, and exported artifacts (CANON-CONTINUITY-CAPSULE-DESIGN.md:507-512).

Drops split into two disjoint classes: `RECORD_ENFORCEABLE = frozenset({CAP_TEMPORAL})` — a lone record can exercise it — and structural (the other four) — a property of the store, not any one record's fields (base.py:50, F1-BACKENDS.md 'The capability model').

Structural drops never raise on a lone put (test_declared_drops.py:73-76).

Error hierarchy roots at `BackendError(Exception)`; three named subclasses: `UnsupportedKind`, `DropError`, `MissingSupersedeTarget` (base.py:53-76). The hierarchy is test-pinned so a caller catches one refusal type (test_backend_base.py:108-111).

CAP_AT_MOST_ONCE = 'at-most-once' — the transport guarantees no duplicate delivery.
CAP_AT_LEAST_ONCE = 'at-least-once' — the transport may deliver twice; caller dedupes by idempotency_key. Mutually exclusive with at-most-once (test-enforced).
CAP_IDEMPOTENT_PUSH = 'idempotent-push' — a duplicate push with a matching idempotency_key is a no-op returning the same Receipt.
CAP_ORDERING_PRESERVING = 'ordering-preserving' — the transport preserves create_ord ordering across a batch.
CAP_REPLAY_SAFE = 'replay-safe' — the transport rejects a matching idempotency_key that carries different bytes (raises DuplicatePush).
CAP_TOMBSTONES = 'tombstones' — transport can carry a delete. OUT at M4 close but the token is reserved.
CAP_STREAMABLE = 'streamable' — transport supports incremental fetch. OUT at M4 close but the token is reserved.
CAP_OFFLINE_SAFE = 'offline-safe' — transport degrades to a local-only mode when the remote is unreachable rather than blocking.
CAP_AUDIT_CHAIN = 'audit-chain' — transport preserves a hash chain across dispatches (mirror F1 CAP_AUDIT_CHAIN).
CAP_FOREIGN_ENVELOPE = 'foreign-envelope' — transport preserves the exact canonical JSON bytes of the envelope end-to-end (byte-identical re-derivation on the far side).

CAP_SCHEMA_PIN_VERIFIED = 'schema-pin-verified' — transport surfaces its schema pin via pin() and refuses a mismatched envelope pin before send (not a drop; every M4 transport MUST advertise this since the pin is part of the seam contract).
TRANSPORT_CAPABILITIES = frozenset({every token above}); every declared_drops entry and every caps entry MUST be a subset of this frozenset (test-pinned).
RECORD_ENFORCEABLE_TRANSPORT = frozenset({temporal-preserving, provenance-preserving, sized-payload-limit}); guard_push raises only on this class.
refusal_types: TransportError(Exception) — root. Every subclass MUST inherit from it. Test-pinned by test_transport_error_hierarchy (mirrors test_backend_base:108-111).
UnsupportedKind(TransportError) — canon-side, raised by guard_push at the top of push(). When the record.kind is not in transport.supported_kinds(). Mirror F1.

DropError(TransportError) — canon-side, raised by guard_push. When the record exercises a record-enforceable capability the transport dropped and the caller did not flatten first (temporal-preserving or provenance-preserving). Mirror F1 D-8.

SchemaMismatch(TransportError) — canon-side, raised by guard_push (send path: envelope.pin != transport.pin()) OR by the wire decoder on fetch (decoded canon_schema != transport.pin()). Cannot be flattened; the fix is a version-pinned migration. Rides D-N of the pins seam.

CapabilityRefused(TransportError) — canon-side, raised by the Protocol method wrapper when the caller invoked push_many/fetch_many on a transport whose caps() lacks remote-batch. Distinct from DropError because it is a wiring fault, not a record loss.

ContentTooLarge(TransportError) — canon-side pre-check by guard_push; may also be raised by the wire decoder on fetch if a returned payload exceeds descriptor.size_limit_bytes; may also be wrapped from a handle-side quota refusal.

PayloadCorrupt(TransportError) — canon-side, raised by the wire decoder on fetch when the returned bytes fail Record.from_dict, canonicalization round-trip, or the sha256 idempotency-key re-derivation. Never propagate the raw json.JSONDecodeError.

IdentityMismatch(TransportError) — canon-side, raised by the wire decoder on fetch when the record's derived record_key does not match the key the caller asked for (mirror the vault spoof rule R2 D-30, projected onto the transport). Analogous to vault_mirror's _require_canon_at spoof refusal.

DuplicatePush(TransportError) — canon-side (if the fake handle detected it) OR wrapped handle-side (if the real handle detected it). Only meaningful when caps() contains replay-safe. When the transport receives a matching idempotency_key with different envelope bytes.

Unreachable(TransportError) — WRAPPED from handle-side. Any connection/socket/timeout exception from the injected handle wraps into this. canon never lets a raw OSError, ConnectionError, or TimeoutError escape.
AuthRefused(TransportError) — WRAPPED from handle-side. Any 401/403/OAuth-refused exception from the injected handle wraps into this. canon does not implement the auth flow itself.

RateLimited(TransportError) — WRAPPED from handle-side. Any 429 / quota-refused exception from the handle wraps into this. Contains a retry_after: int | None field for advisory delay (canon does not sleep).

RemoteRefused(TransportError) — WRAPPED from handle-side. Catch-all for a handle-side refusal that is not any of the above (e.g. a 5xx or a peer NACK). Preserves the handle's error text as .cause_text for the caller to log.
OUT AT M4 CLOSE:
TombstonedRecord — no tombstone kind exists at F0/M4; would need canon.tombstone/v1 (Wave 2). Honest_null.
NotFound — fetch returns None on miss (F1 parity, test-enforced). Never a raise. Honest_null.
ClockSkew — canon has no wall-clock authority (F0 rule: create_time is never authoritative). If a handle reports clock skew, canon wraps it as Unreachable or RemoteRefused. Honest_null.

decisions_to_record: D-N — transport is a Protocol seam, not a live server. Every wire (socket, HTTP, OAuth, TLS, MCP, stdio) stays in the relay repo behind a separate deploy-go.

D-N — capability split: three record-enforceable tokens (temporal-preserving, provenance-preserving, sized-payload-limit) versus every other structural token. Only record-enforceable tokens can raise DropError on a lone push (mirror F1 D-8 grammar).
D-N — refuse-not-flatten discipline holds on the transport side. The caller opts into a record-enforceable loss by calling flatten() first, then push().

D-N — external transport engines are reached through an INJECTED duck-typed handle (canon imports no relay package, no socket module, no HTTP client). Each adapter declares a sibling Protocol RelayHandle / StdioHandle / QueueHandle with only the methods it actually calls. Verified by an import-graph grep in the conformance suite.

D-N — TransportEnvelope, Receipt, and TransportDescriptor are runtime frozen dataclasses, NOT versioned schema artifacts. Wave-1 schemas (canon.capsule/v1, canon.transform-receipt/v1, canon.adapter/v1) stay out of M4.
D-N — canonical serialization is Record.to_json() (json.dumps sort_keys=True) verbatim. No new canonical form; the seam speaks the F0 canonical form.

D-N — idempotency_key = sha256(('canon-transport/v1\n' + record.to_json()).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest(). Domain-separated from vault's 'canon-vault/v1\n' (D-29) so a note-name digest and a transport-key digest cannot collide even by construction.
D-N — fetch(missing) returns None; NEVER raise on miss (mirror F1 backend.get rule). Every backend adapter has this test today; the transport must too.
D-N — list_keys / list_all return unordered lists; determinism is the caller's job (mirror F1 records()).
D-N — NO ClockSkew refusal. canon has no wall-clock authority (F0 rule: create_time is nullable and never authoritative). A handle that reports clock skew is wrapped as Unreachable or RemoteRefused.
D-N — NO delete(), NO tombstone semantics in M4. Would need canon.tombstone/v1 (Wave-2).
D-N — NO exists(), NO health(), NO close() in the Protocol. Composable / not applicable / handle owns lifecycle.
D-N — TransportDescriptor is a lite frozen dataclass, NOT canon.adapter/v1. Wave-1 stays out.

D-N — guard_push runs validate_record on the record. Closes the audit-found FilesBackend.put gap where guard_put ran but validate_record did not — SEC finding SEC-Critical-1 is not repeated on the transport side.

D-N — the conformance suite is fixture-driven, parametrizes over a TransportFactory, and is reusable by any concrete adapter (in-tree or out-of-tree). It exercises every refusal branch against the canon-owned FakeRelayHandle.

D-N — pin() returns a plain str (canon.schema.SCHEMA by default). Not semver-shaped, not compared by version-arithmetic; only literal-equality mismatch is a refusal. Semver is Wave-2 (COMMUNITY-RELEASE-PILLAR-AUDIT recommended-versioning).

D-N — the seam is total on the read side (fetch returns None on miss; list_keys returns [] on empty scope; every refusal on decode raises TransportError). It is loud on the write side (push raises TransportError on any refusal; NEVER silently drops).

D-N — every handle-side exception is wrapped as a TransportError subclass; canon NEVER lets a raw OSError / ValueError / json.JSONDecodeError escape the seam (mirror mneme.py:104-105 ValueError wrapping).
D-N — caps() and declared_drops() are disjoint by post-init check; enforced by test_caps_and_declared_drops_are_disjoint.
D-N — every entry in caps() and declared_drops() MUST be a member of TRANSPORT_CAPABILITIES (mirror test_declared_drops:54-56).
D-N — the fake mirrors the actual relay handle surface read from source this session (mirror F1 D-11). Every knob wired to a specific refusal-branch test.
D-N — Receipt carries (idempotency_key, name, pin) plus optional create_ord echo. Ordering reconstruction under network reorder is caller-inferable via create_ord.

D-N — schema.SCHEMA and backends/base.py are unchanged. The transport package is additive; no F0/F1 API breaks. Backward compatibility gate: run the full 407-test F0-through-V4 suite green before landing M4.

D-N — decisions recorded in project-docs/M4-TRANSPORT-DECISIONS.md; every drop cited to real code with line + confidence in project-docs/M4-TRANSPORT.md (mirror F0-DECLARED-DROPS.md and F1-BACKENDS.md style).
dependencies_on_other_m4_modules: canon.transport is INDEPENDENT of canon.vault_frontend — no cross-import; the vault leg is the read half of R2, the transport leg is the cross-provider seam. Each ships on its own branch, each testable in isolation.

refusal_types: REFUSED_MISSING_FENCE — no leading '---' fence; frontmatter.parse_frontmatter raises FrontmatterError; folded to verdict; catches BOM-at-head, empty file, zero-byte frontmatter
REFUSED_UNCLOSED_FENCE — leading '---' present but no matching '---' before EOF; FrontmatterError folded
REFUSED_NO_CANON_KEY — fenced block carries zero canon: lines; FrontmatterError folded (D-27: carrier is authoritative, absence is refusal)
REFUSED_MULTIPLE_CANON_KEYS — two canon: lines in the fence; FrontmatterError folded (prevents ambiguous authority)
REFUSED_MALFORMED_SCALAR — canon: value not the '<JSON>' single-quoted scalar shape; FrontmatterError folded
REFUSED_INVALID_JSON — canon: payload not a valid JSON document after '' unescape; json.loads raised, folded
REFUSED_INVALID_SCHEMA — payload lacks canon_schema == 'canon.record/v1', or missing structural key (kind/id/scope/data/provenance); Record.from_dict / KeyError / ValueError folded
REFUSED_INVALID_RECORD — validate_record returned problems (unknown kind, unknown scope, wrong data shape, research-artifact-ref carrying temporal); folded to verdict
REFUSED_SPOOF — derive_note_name(record) casefold-differs from the on-disk relpath; matches vault_mirror._discover_orphans spoof rule (D-30) but returned as verdict, not raise
REFUSED_MIS_SCOPE — record.scope does not match the scope directory the file lives in; mirrors R1 D-18 mis-scope refusal
REFUSED_DUPLICATE_KEY — two loaded records share record_key(record) = f'{scope}/{id}'; folded aggregate refusal (mirror of vault_mirror._render_targets' duplicate raise, but as verdict)
SKIPPED_HUB — the top-level MEMORY.md is a projection per D-27/D-32/D-34 and never a source; skipped without content check

SKIPPED_NOT_ALLOWED — is_vault_write_allowed refused the path: root itself, '..' escape, absolute path outside root, top-level non-hub file, ad-hoc deeper-than-scope path, unknown scope directory, cross-drive/mixed-abs-rel (ValueError caught)
SKIPPED_ABSENT — read_text(path) returned None between listing and read; listing raced a delete
SKIPPED_NOT_MARKDOWN — dotfile (.hidden.md), .md.bak, .md.tmp, or a scope-level directory entry lacking .md suffix; falls out of is_vault_write_allowed

edge_cases_covered.case: spoofed filename that does not re-derive (hostile id took over a legitimate note's slot)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: REFUSED_SPOOF: normcase(derive_note_name(record)) != normcase(relpath); returned as verdict, never raised (contrast: vault_mirror raises here)

edge_cases_covered.case: canon: key stripped from an otherwise well-formed frontmatter
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: parse_frontmatter counts zero canon: lines -> FrontmatterError -> REFUSED_NO_CANON_KEY

edge_cases_covered.case: canon: key present but the JSON is invalid (trailing comma, bad quote, NaN literal)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: json.loads raises -> REFUSED_INVALID_JSON; fold ValueError inside classify_vault_entry

edge_cases_covered.case: canon: JSON parses but is not a record shape (missing kind, wrong canon_schema string)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: Record.from_dict raises KeyError or ValueError -> REFUSED_INVALID_SCHEMA

edge_cases_covered.case: oversized frontmatter (multi-megabyte canon: payload as a DoS vector)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: HONEST NULL: no size ceiling in M4 (SECURITY-PRIVACY-THREAT-MODEL.md flags as owed). The reader passes the string through; a caller's read_text may impose a ceiling by returning None or raising above threshold — the seam accepts either without change

edge_cases_covered.case: trailing junk after the closing frontmatter fence (attacker appends fake headings, links, code fences)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: IGNORED per D-27: parse_frontmatter reads only the fenced block, ingest_note uses only the canon: JSON; body/junk never touched

edge_cases_covered.case: BOM at file head (utf-8-sig style)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: REFUSED_MISSING_FENCE: line 0 becomes '﻿---' not '---'; NO silent BOM strip (matches R2 region.py byte-discipline: never open with utf-8-sig, BOM stays an ordinary prefix)

edge_cases_covered.case: CRLF newlines throughout the note (a Windows editor saved it)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: _normalize (mirroring vault_mirror._normalize) converts CRLF->LF and bare CR->LF before parse; note reconstructs byte-identically to its LF twin

edge_cases_covered.case: LF newlines (native canon shape)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: _normalize is a no-op; parsed directly

edge_cases_covered.case: mixed newlines within one file (CRLF header, LF body, bare CR sprinkled)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: _normalize applies CRLF then bare-CR replacement; single canonical form fed to parser

edge_cases_covered.case: symlink whose target escapes the root
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: HONEST NULL: canon does no realpath check (matches R2 D-31 lexical-only posture). The injected list_dir decides whether to follow symlinks; canon's containment is lexical. Documented in module docstring and vault_reader.md

edge_cases_covered.case: absolute path handed as a listing entry (attacker-supplied list_dir returns an absolute)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: SKIPPED_NOT_ALLOWED: is_vault_write_allowed refuses (commonpath check fails or parts count > 2)

edge_cases_covered.case: root itself listed as a note path
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: SKIPPED_NOT_ALLOWED: is_vault_write_allowed returns False when target == root

edge_cases_covered.case: MEMORY.md hub counted as a note (attacker wraps hub as a fake record)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: SKIPPED_HUB: relpath match on _HUB_RELPATH short-circuits before parse; no attempt to ingest hub; matches D-27/D-32/D-34 non-durable-hub rule

edge_cases_covered.case: dotfile at note position (.hidden.md, .DS_Store)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: SKIPPED_NOT_ALLOWED: is_vault_write_allowed refuses (parts[1] does not endswith '.md' in a canon-recognized way; dotfiles fall out of the two-part scope/*.md shape)

edge_cases_covered.case: .md.bak / .md.tmp editor backups
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: SKIPPED_NOT_ALLOWED via endswith('.md') check; .bak/.tmp fall out

edge_cases_covered.case: wrong-scope directory placement (a record with scope='workspace' lives under global/foo-<digest>.md)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: REFUSED_MIS_SCOPE: after ingest, record.scope != parts[0]; mirrors R1 D-18 mis-scope refusal

edge_cases_covered.case: two files whose derive_note_name digest collides (sha256 truncation collision — cryptographically implausible, but present as a rule)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: REFUSED_DUPLICATE_KEY or REFUSED_SPOOF depending on which id 'owns' the path; at least one is refused; matches vault_mirror._render_targets collision refusal

edge_cases_covered.case: unicode NFC vs NFD filename collision (composed vs decomposed accents)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: derive_note_name uses NFKD-then-ASCII-drop in _slugify; the same input id always slugs the same way. normcase(on-disk) is compared to normcase(derive_note_name(record)); NFC/NFD variants of the same id produce identical derived names, and any mismatch is REFUSED_SPOOF

edge_cases_covered.case: non-ASCII in name that renders differently from derive (attacker's filename has fullwidth chars a legitimate slug would not)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: REFUSED_SPOOF: derived name uses NFKD+ASCII-only slug, so fullwidth diverges; folded to verdict

edge_cases_covered.case: empty file (0 bytes)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: lines[0] is '' not '---' -> REFUSED_MISSING_FENCE

edge_cases_covered.case: zero-byte frontmatter (immediate closing fence: '---\n---\n')
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: parse_frontmatter counts zero canon: lines -> REFUSED_NO_CANON_KEY

edge_cases_covered.case: frontmatter without matching closing marker
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: REFUSED_UNCLOSED_FENCE

edge_cases_covered.case: note with two canon: keys (attacker injects a second one)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: REFUSED_MULTIPLE_CANON_KEYS: parse_frontmatter raises when count != 1

edge_cases_covered.case: canon: key at wrong position within the fence (last line instead of first)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: IGNORED — parse_frontmatter scans every line in the fence and matches the one starting with 'canon: \''; position within fence does not matter; loads normally

edge_cases_covered.case: hand-edited body under an intact carrier (user edited the prose, not the JSON)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: LOADED cleanly per D-27: ingest_note reads only the canon: JSON; body/heading/trailer/aliases ignored. The record returned is the one the carrier declares, not what the body says

edge_cases_covered.case: orphan note not indexed by any hub entry
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: LOADED: hub is a projection per D-32; the read leg does not consult the hub at all; every canon-owned note is a source

edge_cases_covered.case: orphan hub entry pointing at a missing note
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: IRRELEVANT — hub is skipped as a source; the reader never reads a hub link

edge_cases_covered.case: foreign MEMORY.md (hand-authored, no canon head)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: SKIPPED_HUB anyway; the reader does not verify the hub head (that's write-leg ownership); mirrors read-only totality

edge_cases_covered.case: !!python/object YAML injection in body or in a decoy YAML tag
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: INERT: no YAML loader runs; frontmatter reader uses string scan + json.loads on the canon: line alone. Trap fires nowhere. Test explicitly with the pyyaml-crashing payload

edge_cases_covered.case: bare CR anywhere in a note that a hostile editor saved
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: _normalize converts to LF before parse; the record round-trips. If the carrier's JSON payload contains a CR (only possible if a hostile writer forged one), Record.from_dict / render_note fidelity refuses on next round trip

edge_cases_covered.case: case-only path variant on a case-insensitive filesystem (Foo-<digest>.md vs foo-<digest>.md)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: normcase folds both to same path; recognized as the SAME target (not a spoof). Mirrors vault_mirror._discover_orphans normcase logic

edge_cases_covered.case: two distinct records with the same (scope, id) — duplicate record_key across two note files
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: REFUSED_DUPLICATE_KEY: aggregate-phase check after all loaded verdicts collected; deterministic first-wins by sorted(list_dir) order; both files reported in refusal reason

edge_cases_covered.case: ad-hoc deeper-than-scope path (global/subdir/note.md)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: SKIPPED_NOT_ALLOWED: is_vault_write_allowed requires exactly 2 path parts

edge_cases_covered.case: top-level non-MEMORY.md file (root-level README.md a user added)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: SKIPPED_NOT_ALLOWED: len(parts)==1 but parts[0] != normcase(MEMORY.md)

edge_cases_covered.case: concurrent-change during listing (a file disappears between list_dir and read_text)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: SKIPPED_ABSENT: read_text returns None; classify_vault_entry never runs on an absent file; caller does not see a KeyError

edge_cases_covered.case: list_dir raises OSError (permission denied on a subdir)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: HONEST NULL: propagates. The IO contract says list_dir yields; an OS error is the caller's; canon does not swallow it (matches drift.py's read_text contract)

edge_cases_covered.case: workspace note under global/ AND global note under workspace/ (attacker cross-shuffles)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: Both REFUSED_MIS_SCOPE independently; per-entry verdicts; aggregate ok=False

edge_cases_covered.case: very large vault (10k+ notes)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: iter_notes streams one verdict at a time; find_by_predicate composes over the iterator; memory footprint is O(1) per record; only the aggregate pool for read_vault materializes all loaded records

edge_cases_covered.case: wikilink-hostile id in a legitimate carrier ('topic#v2', 'bad]id')
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: LOADED: reader ignores aliases and body entirely (D-27); reconstruction is from carrier JSON alone; the derived filename uses _link_token's fallback slug-plus-digest, matched via normcase(derive_note_name)

edge_cases_covered.case: Windows reserved names in a derived filename (CON, NUL) — theoretically possible if the id slugs to a reserved word
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: The trailing sha256 suffix defuses collision with a real reserved name; the reader accepts the actual on-disk name because the spoof check re-derives via the same domain-tagged digest

edge_cases_covered.case: duplicate hub entries pointing to spoof notes (attacker mismatches hub)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: IRRELEVANT — reader ignores the hub; only actual note files matter

edge_cases_covered.case: listing entry with backslashes on POSIX (relpath contains \)
edge_cases_covered.mechanism: Consistent with vault_mirror._discover_orphans: replace('\\', '/') normalizes before path checks; then is_vault_write_allowed decides

honest_nulls: Real filesystem walking is NOT provided (caller injects list_dir; canon imports no os.walk / pathlib). Reason: matches R1/R2 injected-IO discipline and V4 D-63/D-64 path-clean posture.

Symlink/junction/reparse-point resolution is NOT performed (lexical containment only). Reason: R2 D-31 stance carried forward; realpath would open a new attack surface and require an OS call canon does not own.

File-lock / cross-process CAS is NOT provided. Reason: V4 D-66 disclosed non-transactional boundary; M4 read leg is read-only IO-injected and cannot coordinate writers. Caller must supply a consistent list_dir/read_text pair (e.g. snapshot-based).
Watch/notify / inotify / FSEvents semantics are NOT provided. Reason: canon has no runtime dependency and no event-loop story; a caller can wrap the reader in its own watcher.

Remote-vault transport (fetch a vault over the network) is NOT provided. Reason: transport is out of M4 vault-frontend scope and the operator ceiling forbids sockets/HTTP/OAuth; live tunnel lives in the relay repo behind a separate deploy-go.

Vault mutation (writing, deleting, moving notes) is NOT provided. Reason: R2 D-32 (orphan reported never deleted) and the write leg (vault_mirror.plan_vault) own that surface; the read leg is read-only.
Git integration (commit hooks, per-branch views, blame overlay) is NOT provided. Reason: canon is provider-neutral and stdlib-only; git is a caller concern.
Editor integration (Obsidian-plugin bridge, LSP surface) is NOT provided. Reason: out of M4 scope; a plugin can wrap the seam.

Per-note byte-size ceiling / oversized-frontmatter refusal is NOT enforced. Reason: SECURITY-PRIVACY-THREAT-MODEL.md flags as an owed hardening; M4 keeps the reader minimal and lets a caller's read_text impose a limit by returning None or raising above threshold.

BOM-tolerant read mode is NOT provided. Reason: R2 byte-discipline (region.py D-12) forbids silent BOM strip; a BOM makes the fence check fail and produces REFUSED_MISSING_FENCE, which is the intended honest verdict.
MEMORY.md content validation is NOT performed (hub is skipped without inspection). Reason: D-27/D-32/D-34: the hub is a projection, not a record; the write leg owns hub ownership checks.
Merge across two vault roots is NOT provided. Reason: single-root by construction; a caller who wants a union may compose two read_vault results manually.
Character-set validation of note bodies is NOT performed. Reason: D-27: body is a one-way projection ignored on read; body bytes never influence the record.
Concurrency snapshot / mid-read atomicity is NOT provided. Reason: no runtime dependency policy; the injected IO shape can be pointed at a snapshot (e.g. copytree) by the caller.
Realpath-based traversal defense is NOT provided (only lexical). Reason: R2 D-31 posture — the same rule that governs the write leg governs the read leg.
Hub-orphan cross-check (does every hub link resolve to a note?) is NOT provided. Reason: hub is a projection; the reader does not consult it.
Namespaced vault (multiple canon roots side-by-side under one parent) is NOT provided as a first-class shape. Reason: a caller may call read_vault once per root and union the results.
Delta / incremental read (only what changed since a prior snapshot) is NOT provided. Reason: no persistent snapshot store; would require Wave 1 witness schema that is out of M4.

D-70 — read leg is total; every refusal is a NoteVerdict, never raised (parity with V2 drift D-42 and V4 classify D-56). Consequence: read_exit_code, aggregate ok bit, and a CI gate that can key on exit-status without try/except.

D-78 — no new schema artifacts, no CLI, no capability tokens beyond what F1/R2 already speak. Consequence: M4 stays a plumbing band; Wave 1 schemas remain out. STATUSES is a closed frozenset (no runtime widening) and any unknown status is a wiring fault, not a silent verdict.

api_surface: SEAM_PINS: frozenset[str] — closed vocabulary of pin short-names {'record','backend-seam','textblock-grammar','region-marker','frontmatter','vault-note','drift-verdict','writing-gate-register','persona-thesis-payload','reconcile-gate-policy','run-witness','transport-seam','vault-frontend'}. Every PIN_REGISTRY key must be a member; test_every_registry_key_is_in_seam_pins pins it (mirrors F1 CAPABILITIES).

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class SchemaPin: name: str, version: str, kind_tag: str, adr_ref: str. __post_init__ validates name in SEAM_PINS, version matches ^v[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$, kind_tag has exactly one '/', adr_ref non-empty — same edge-guard discipline as ConflictGatePolicy.__post_init__.

PIN_REGISTRY: MappingProxyType[str, SchemaPin] — read-only view over the module-level dict populated once at import. Public reads via pin_for/all_pins. Direct assignment raises TypeError; the pin_registry_scope contextmanager is the only write path outside module init.

PIN_RECORD, PIN_BACKEND_SEAM, PIN_TEXTBLOCK_GRAMMAR, PIN_REGION_MARKER, PIN_FRONTMATTER, PIN_VAULT_NOTE, PIN_DRIFT_VERDICT, PIN_WRITING_GATE_REGISTER, PIN_PERSONA_THESIS_PAYLOAD, PIN_RECONCILE_GATE_POLICY, PIN_RUN_WITNESS, PIN_TRANSPORT_SEAM, PIN_VAULT_FRONTEND: module-level SchemaPin constants — the handles callers reference by name, never by string literal.
def pin_for(name: str) -> SchemaPin — refuses UnknownPin on a name not in SEAM_PINS; message names the sorted vocabulary.
def all_pins() -> tuple[SchemaPin, ...] — byte-stable sorted-by-name tuple (mirrors R2 sorted(targets) discipline). Fresh tuple each call, identical contents.
def describe(pin: SchemaPin) -> str — pure formatter: 'name @ kind_tag (adr_ref)'. No registry lookup, no IO.

def is_compatible(theirs: SchemaPin, ours: SchemaPin) -> bool — semver-lite policy: at v0/v1 exact equality on (name, version, kind_tag). Refuses MalformedPin when either arg is not a SchemaPin. Widening path for v2+ documented, not implemented (honest null).
def pin_from_schema_field(schema_str: str) -> SchemaPin — linear scan matching on kind_tag. Refuses UnknownPin when no pin matches; refuses MalformedPin on empty / newline-bearing / bad-shape input.
class MigrationFn(Protocol): __call__(record: Record) -> Record — duck-typed migrator shape. Zero migrators ship at M4 close because no cross-version records exist.

def register_migrator(from_pin: SchemaPin, to_pin: SchemaPin, fn: MigrationFn) -> None — installs into module-level _MIGRATORS dict keyed by (SchemaPin, SchemaPin). Refuses UnknownPin on unregistered pins; refuses MigratorConflict on duplicate (from, to) pair — explicit-or-refuse, no silent overwrite.
def unregister_migrator(from_pin: SchemaPin, to_pin: SchemaPin) -> None — idempotent remove for test cleanup; missing entry is a no-op, not a refusal.

def migrate(record: Record, from_pin: SchemaPin, to_pin: SchemaPin) -> Record — identity when from_pin == to_pin (fast path, no lookup). Otherwise calls registered migrator; refuses IncompatiblePin with no migrator registered.

class pin_registry_scope (contextmanager) — snapshots PIN_REGISTRY and _MIGRATORS at __enter__, yields writable view, restores on __exit__ via try/finally (including on exception). The scope is the ONLY write path outside module init. Same discipline as F1 D-11 fake-mirror isolation.

refusal_types: VersionError(Exception) — root of the family; naming matches BackendError / VaultError / LayeringError / RegionError.

UnknownPin(VersionError) — raised by pin_for on a name not in SEAM_PINS; by register_migrator on an unregistered pin; by pin_from_schema_field when no registered kind_tag matches. Message names the offending value and the sorted vocabulary.

IncompatiblePin(VersionError) — raised by migrate when from_pin != to_pin and no migrator is registered. Message names both pins and cites register_migrator as the fix — the seam is explicit-migrator-or-refuse.
MalformedPin(VersionError) — raised by is_compatible when either arg is not a SchemaPin (Protocol shape violation); by pin_from_schema_field on empty / newline-bearing / bad-shape schema_str.

MigratorConflict(ValueError, VersionError) — raised by register_migrator when a migrator already exists for that (from_pin, to_pin) key. Multi-inherits ValueError for callers already catching that. Cleared via unregister_migrator.

ValueError (SchemaPin.__post_init__) — refused at construction on: name outside SEAM_PINS; version not matching semver-lite regex; kind_tag empty or lacking exactly one '/'; adr_ref empty. Loud fault at the edge.

ValueError (reconcile_action-style out-of-vocabulary) — not raised by this module but the discipline is inherited: an out-of-vocabulary resolution in the migration protocol would surface at the wiring boundary, not silently pass through.

honest_nulls: No semver policy negotiation between peers — the seam is a local pin registry; a distributed handshake is out.

No RFC-style public spec publication — the pin table lives in project-docs as internal docs; publication is a separate band.
No conformance CLI — no `canon conform --pin record` entrypoint; the approval note bans CLI in M4.
No docs site — deferred.
No migrators registered at M4 close — no cross-version records exist yet, so register_migrator has nothing to install. The seam ships empty, verified by test_no_migrators_registered_at_m4_close.
No v2+ pins at M4 close — every SchemaPin ships at v0 or v1 (record=v1; every new seam pin=v0). The v2+ widening path is documented in is_compatible's docstring but never exercised.
No cross-pin migration runtime beyond the Protocol — migrate refuses without a registered migrator; no reflection-based migrator inference, no field-diff generator, no schema-aware transformer.

No Wave-1 schema pins — canon.atom/v1, canon.capsule/v1, canon.omission/v1, canon.transform-receipt/v1, canon.readiness-probe/v1, canon.bootstrap-witness/v1, canon.adapter/v1 explicitly excluded. Pinned by test_seam_pins_excludes_wave_one and test_pin_for_wave_one_names_all_refuse.

No production vault_frontend module — versions.py declares PIN_VAULT_FRONTEND but the whole-vault reader Protocol lands in M4.2, not here.
No live-cross-provider transport at all in canon — the live tunnel and OAuth live in the relay repo; canon.transport-seam/v0 is a Protocol handle, not a client.
No PyPI/npm/crates package registration — collision audit flagged 'canon' as taken on all three; publishing is a separate deploy-go.
No CLI entrypoint that speaks pins — no argparse main, no `python -m canon.versions`; callers use the library API only.
No wire-format for pins over a network — pins are Python objects; pin_from_schema_field parses only the canon_schema string a record already carries, not a versioned handshake message.
No lifetime tracking for a pin — no deprecation dates, no sunset schedules; a v0-to-v1 bump ships when the next migration record exists (just-in-time discipline).
No trust/signature on pins — a pin is a plain frozen dataclass; the trust label vocabulary (trusted-local, signed-pinned, etc.) is Wave-1 material.
No adapter/tier vocabulary in the pin registry — Enforced/Native-advisory/Guided/Unsupported belongs on canon.adapter/v1 (Wave 1), not here.
No cross-repo pin discovery — canon.versions declares canon's own pins; the relay repo declares its own; a federated registry is out.

No on-disk fixture rewriter — the six fixture JSON files (tests/fixtures/records/*.json + tests/fixtures/layering_pool.json) that carry the literal 'canon.record/v1' at rest are data payloads and are NOT rewritten by M4.
No capability-token machinery on pins — a pin is not a capability. F1 CAPABILITIES ride on the backend-seam pin but are not pins themselves.
No persistence, no DB, no file-backed registry — the registry is a module-level dict populated at import; nothing crosses process boundaries.

No thread-safety promise beyond stdlib defaults — pin_registry_scope uses a threading.Lock around snapshot/restore, but the registry itself is not designed for concurrent mutation from multiple threads. Test coverage is single-threaded.

No integration with F1 backend Protocol's `capabilities` — a backend that returns capabilities does not need to declare pin_for('backend-seam') in its return; version handshaking between a backend and a caller is a v2+ story.

breaches_of_ceiling: Versions leg's D-numbers D-69..D-79 collide with vault-frontend's D-69..D-78. Prior bands (V2 D-37..D-42, V3 D-43..D-50, V4 D-51..D-68) use unique D-numbers project-wide. Two M4 sub-bands claiming the same D-numbers breaks the accountability contract; the collision is a documentation-ceiling breach, not just a housekeeping typo.

Transport's `Receipt` (or `TransportReceipt`) is described as 'runtime dataclass, not a schema' but it carries `idempotency_key` across process boundaries and is fetched by a remote peer via `fetch_receipt(key)`. Any structure that survives a process boundary and gets fetched by key IS a wire schema in effect, which lands inside Wave 1 (`canon.transform-receipt/v1`). Either name it `canon.transport-receipt/v1` and defer to Wave 1, or drop `fetch_receipt`.

Transport spec's `guard_push` performing a size check on the serialized envelope requires calling `record.to_json()` before knowing the size, which is an ambient allocation an adversary can weaponize. Any 'max byte' policy on injected records edges into a runtime policy artifact (`canon.transport-policy/v1`?) that is out of Wave 1 and out of M4.

Vault-reader spec's `iter_scope_notes` and `find_by_predicate` implicitly define a query language surface. Even a predicate-callable is a Protocol; canon does not have a query Protocol yet, and inventing one in M4 is a schema step, not a plumbing step.

Versions spec's proposal to 'sprinkle SEAM_VERSION = pin_for(<name>) into every module' is a public-API expansion across every existing band (F0, F1, R0, R1, R2, V2, V3, V4). That is not a versioning module — it is a project-wide refactor that touches surfaces already shipped. Approval covered versioning, not editing every band.

Vault-reader spec proposes `plan_read(vault_root)` that traverses arbitrary directories under the injected `list_dir`. The R2 write leg uses lexical containment (`is_vault_write_allowed`) explicitly to avoid needing filesystem realpath — vault-reader must adopt the same lexical stance or it silently gains a filesystem-real-world dependency that the write leg refused.
missing_edge_cases: Transport: at-least-once delivery with the same idempotency_key arriving twice within a single batch (network-reorder duplicate). Spec says peer deduplicates cross-batch; nothing says what happens intra-batch.

Transport: idempotency_key sha256 collision — an honest-null note (collisions are astronomically implausible) is missing. Prior bands (vault D-27) enumerate cryptographic-implausibility cases explicitly.

Transport: `fetch_many` called with the same key twice in the request list — spec returns a dict keyed by key; two identical keys collapse silently. Either refuse duplicate keys, or document the collapse.

Transport: memory-exhaustion trap. `guard_push` computes size AFTER `record.to_json()` allocates the entire envelope. A `record` whose `data` is a giant string OOMs before the size gate can refuse it. Measure a cheap kind-and-data-length heuristic first.

Transport: partial-batch failure. `push_many(records)` — if the 7th of 10 records refuses (unsupported kind, wrong schema), spec is silent on whether the first 6 receipts have already committed on the peer. Prior R1 batch (`write_surfaces`) is explicitly all-or-nothing planned-then-committed. Transport must match or explicitly diverge.
Vault reader: Windows MAX_PATH — a note path over 260 characters on non-`\\?\` prefixed paths fails silently on some Windows configs. The spec addresses symlink loops but not this OS-specific limit.
Vault reader: Windows junction cycle (not the same as a symlink) — junctions predate NTFS symlinks and are handled by a separate API path. Spec's 'symlink loop' guard does not cover them.

Vault reader: UTF-16 or UTF-32 BOM (`\xff\xfe` / `\xfe\xff\x00\x00`). Spec only addresses UTF-8 BOM. A UTF-16 file appears as a note but decodes to garbage under the injected `read_text` if the caller opens as UTF-8. Refuse explicitly.
Vault reader: `read_text` returning `bytes` instead of `str` (caller injected the wrong callable). No type check anywhere; a silent AttributeError deep in `_normalize` is the observable behavior.

Vault reader: iterator held past close. If `list_dir` returns a generator that lazily reads FS and a note is deleted mid-iteration, the reader yields a stale entry. The R2 write leg's plan-then-commit sidesteps this; the read leg does not.

Vault reader: two notes whose `derive_note_name` collide via unicode NFKC (fullwidth chars folded) but differ on disk. The vault codec's `_slugify` uses NFKD-then-ASCII-drop, which is not the same normalization as filesystem lookup. Round-trip returns two distinct file paths for what canon considers one record.
Versions: SchemaPin regex `^v[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$` accepts `v01` (leading zero) and treats `v0.1` and `v00.1` as distinct. Semver-lite policy must explicitly reject leading zeros.
Versions: `v0` vs `v0.0` equality is undefined by the regex. Either normalize both to a canonical form or explicitly refuse `v0.0` and require `v0`.

Versions: pre-release/build metadata (`v0+build.1`, `v0-rc.1`) — the regex silently rejects them. That's the right call for M4, but the refusal path must be a typed error with a message pointing at Wave 2, not a bare `ValueError`.

Versions: `pin_registry_scope` context manager under threaded caller. Spec claims `threading.Lock`, but the guarantee is 'the snapshot on exit restores what was there on entry' — a second thread entering the scope mid-body sees the swapped registry. Either serialize the whole scope or document the thread-locality clearly.

Versions: migration seam — a migrator raising `Exception` (not `MigrationError`) bypasses the guard and reaches the caller as a bare exception. Guard must wrap-and-rethrow the way `MnemeBackend.put` at src/canon/backends/mneme.py:95 wraps engine-native errors.

Versions: `describe(pin)` returns a formatted string that is neither JSON nor sortable and cannot be re-parsed. Downstream drift-tests and reports need a stable machine form; ship `describe(pin, *, form='human'|'json')` or drop `describe`.

Implicit dep risk: Transport's `Receipt` fetching over 'a peer boundary' — if the reference implementation reaches for `pickle`, `json`, or a hash serializer, `pickle` must be forbidden (it is not stdlib-safe across trust boundaries). Add an explicit test that `transport.py` does not import `pickle`.

Implicit dep risk: Versions' `pin_registry_scope` context manager — if it uses `contextvars` for thread-locality (correct choice for asyncio) versus `threading.local`, the choice must be pinned. `contextvars` is stdlib but rarely used elsewhere in canon; a mixed choice will confuse future maintainers.
Vault reader's directory traversal must not import `pathlib.Path.rglob` (which does OS I/O) — it must use the injected `list_dir` recursively. A silent `Path.rglob` import is an ambient-IO leak.
